title: Stater: Lion (obverse); Incuse Punches (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, minted at Miletos (Ionia)
caption: This electrum stater from Miletos pairs a lion with incuse punches. Its metal is an alloy of gold and silver.

title: Stater: Barley (obverse); Barley, Incuse (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, minted at Metapontion (South Italy)
caption: A silver stater from Metapontion shows barley on both faces, with the reverse design incuse.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Tetradrachm: Head of Athena (obverse); Owl (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, minted at Athens (Attica)
caption: Athena and her owl identify this Athenian silver tetradrachm. The letters ΑΘΕ on the reverse abbreviate the city’s name.

title: Stater: Baal (obverse); Head of Pharnabazos (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Iran, Achaemenid (550–330 BCE), minted at Tarsos (Kilikia)
caption: This silver stater was minted at Tarsos under the Achaemenid Empire. Its catalogued subjects are Baal and the head of Pharnabazos.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Punch-Marked Coin
creator: Unrecorded maker; India, Rajasthan, Maurya period (322–185 BCE)
caption: This Indian silver coin belongs to a tradition of cutting metal to weight and marking it with punches. Each piece carried its own combination of symbols.

title: Tetradrachm: Head of Young Herakles (obverse); Zeus (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, Macedonian, minted at Amphipolis (Macedonia), reign of Alexander III [The Great]
caption: The youthful Herakles wears a lion skin on the front of this coin, while Zeus sits on the reverse. Its inscription names Alexander.

title: Tetradrachm Coin of Demetrios I
creator: Unrecorded maker; Afghanistan, Bactria, Indo-Greek
caption: Demetrios I appears wearing an elephant scalp on this silver tetradrachm. Hercules occupies the reverse.

title: Octodrachm: Head of Arsinoe II (obverse); Double Cornucopia (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Greek, Ptolemaic, minted at Alexandreia (Egypt), reign of Ptolemy V Epiphanes or Ptolemy VI Philometor
caption: Arsinoe II wears a crown and veil on this gold octodrachm. A pair of cornucopias appears on its reverse.

title: Ring Money
creator: Unrecorded maker; England
caption: This piece of gold ring money was found at Norman Leighton in Warwickshire. The museum notes that ring money could be strung and carried on the body.

title: Knife Coin
creator: Unrecorded maker; China
caption: This bronze object is catalogued by The Met as a knife coin from China’s Han dynasty. Its elongated form differs from the round coins elsewhere in the collection.
sourceNote: The museum supplies the period Han dynasty (206 BCE–220 CE), but no narrower object date. sortYear 7 is the midpoint used only for gallery ordering.

title: Aureus: Bust of Claudius I (obverse); Triumphal Arch with Equestrian Statue and Trophies (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; England, Roman, Claudius I (41–54 CE)
caption: This gold aureus pairs a portrait of Claudius I with a triumphal arch, an equestrian statue and trophies. The museum dates it to 47–48 CE.

title: Coin
creator: Unrecorded maker; India, Mathura, Kushan period
caption: A gold coin from the reign of the Kushan ruler Havishka. It places a ruler’s portrait on the obverse and a deity on the reverse.

title: Drachm: Bust of Hormizd II (obverse); Fire altar with bust (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Iran, (minted), Sasanian Empire (224–651 CE), reign of Hormizd II (303–309)
caption: This silver drachm dates to the reign of Hormizd II. The museum identifies a royal bust on the obverse and a fire altar with a bust on the reverse.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Coin of Chandragupta II
creator: Unrecorded maker; India, Chandragupta II, Gupta Period, late 4th-early 5th century
caption: This gold coin of Chandragupta II depicts an archer carrying a bow and arrow. Shri, the goddess of good fortune, sits on a lotus on the reverse.

title: Tremissis of Honorius
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium, Ravenna, Byzantine period, late 4th-early 5th Century
caption: The museum identifies this gold coin as a tremissis of Honorius, minted at Ravenna. A tremissis was one third of a solidus in weight and value.

title: Drachm: Bust of Napki Malka (obverse): Fire Altar (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; Hephtalite, minted in Afghanistan, reign of Napki Malka
caption: A silver drachm catalogued to the reign of Napki Malka in Afghanistan. Its two sides show a ruler’s bust and a fire altar.
sourceNote: Caption is limited to the museum’s title, date, medium and cultural attribution; no extended object description is supplied.

title: Solidus of Justinian I
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium, Constantinople, Byzantine period
caption: This solidus represents Justinian I and was minted at Constantinople. The gold solidus was a standard denomination of Byzantine coinage.

title: Witmen Tremissis: Bust and Trident (obverse); Cross Fourchée (reverse)
creator: Unrecorded maker; England, Anglo-Saxon, early 7th century
caption: This early seventh-century gold tremissis follows the Witmen type. It pairs a bust and trident with a forked cross.

title: Solidus with Heraclius and his Son Heraclius Constantine
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium
caption: This gold solidus depicts Heraclius and his son Heraclius Constantine. Byzantine coins increasingly represented heirs and co-emperors alongside the ruler.

title: Nomisma with Nicephorus II Phocas
creator: Unrecorded maker; Byzantium
caption: This gold nomisma represents Nicephorus II Phocas. The museum dates it to about 963–969, during the century when the nomisma replaced the solidus as the standard gold coin.

title: Dinar of Mahmud
creator: Unknown mint; present-day Afghanistan
caption: A gold dinar bearing the name of Mahmud, dated 419 AH / 1028 CE. The museum catalogues it among its Islamic coins.

title: Nomisma with Constantine IX Monomachus
creator: Byzantium
caption: A Byzantine gold nomisma associated with Constantine IX Monomachus. The museum dates this coin to his reign, 1042–1055.

title: Dinar of Tughril
creator: Nishapur, Iran
caption: A gold dinar of Tughril, dated 444 AH / 1052–53 CE. The museum identifies its place of production as Nishapur.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Dinar of Tughril (r. 1040–63)

title: Dirham with a Double-Headed Bird of Prey
creator: Hisn Kayfa, present-day Turkey
caption: This copper dirham of Nasir al-Din Mahmud carries a double-headed bird of prey. It is dated 615 AH / 1218–19 CE.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Dirham of Nasir al-Din Mahmud (r. 1201–22): Double-Headed Bird of Prey

title: Dirham with the Sun and Lion
creator: Konya, present-day Turkey
caption: A silver dirham of Ghiyath al-Din Kai Khusrau II, with the sun-and-lion device named in the museum record. It is dated 638 AH / 1240–41 CE.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Dirham of Ghiyath al-Din Kai Khusrau II (r. 1239–46); Astrological Device (Sun-Lion)

title: Mouton d'Or of Jean le Bon
creator: France
caption: A gold coin from the reign of King Jean le Bon of France. The museum dates this Gothic-period example to 1350–1364.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Mouton d'Or of King Jean le Bon of France, 1350-1364

title: Noble of Edward III
creator: England
caption: Edward III stands in a ship on one face; an ornamental cross appears on the other. The noble was the first English gold coin struck in substantial numbers.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Noble: Edward III Standing in Ship with Shield of Arms (obverse); Ornamental Cross with Lis Terminals (reverse)

title: A Goldsmith in his Shop
creator: Petrus Christus
caption: A goldsmith weighs a ring before a couple, with coins and precious wares in his shop. The Met interprets the scene as a portrayal of the profession, perhaps of a particular Bruges craftsman.

title: Death and the Miser
creator: Hieronymus Bosch
caption: At the miser’s deathbed, a demon offers a money bag while an angel directs him toward a crucifix. Bosch frames accumulated wealth as a moral temptation.

title: The Merchant and his Wife
creator: Marinus van Reymerswale
caption: A merchant and his wife sit with coins, scales and a ledger. SMK interprets the scene as a warning against greed.
sourceNote: English title for the museum’s Danish title Købmanden med sin kone; artist spelling follows SMK.

title: Halfcrown of Elizabeth I
creator: England
caption: This gold halfcrown pairs a portrait of Elizabeth I with a crowned shield of arms. The museum dates it to 1560–61.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Halfcrown: Elizabeth I (obverse); Crowned Shield of Arms (reverse)

title: The Merchant Robbed by Monkeys
creator: Pieter van der Heyden; After Pieter Bruegel the Elder
caption: A merchant is robbed by monkeys in this engraving after Pieter Bruegel the Elder. The Met dates it to 1562 and identifies Hieronymus Cock as its publisher.

title: The Battle about Money
creator: Pieter van der Heyden; After Pieter Bruegel the Elder
caption: Armed money bags, coin-filled barrels and treasure chests wage a chaotic battle. The Met connects this image after Bruegel with the destructive pursuit of wealth.

title: Coin with Gemini Zodiac Sign
creator: India
caption: A silver coin from India bearing the zodiac sign Gemini. The museum dates it to 1027 AH / 1618 CE.

title: Coin with Sign of Libra
creator: Agra, India
caption: A gold coin bearing the sign of Libra, dated 1034 AH / 1625 CE. The museum identifies Agra as its place of production.

title: Christ Driving the Money Changers from the Temple
creator: Rembrandt (Rembrandt van Rijn)
caption: Rembrandt depicts Christ driving money changers from the temple in this 1635 etching.

title: Jan Uytenbogaert, “The Goldweigher”
creator: Rembrandt van Rijn
caption: Tax collector Jan Uytenbogaert receives payments at his counting table. He was also Rembrandt’s friend and a patron of the arts.

title: Byrsa Londinensis vulgo the Royal Exchange (Royal Exchange, London)
creator: Wenceslaus Hollar
medium: Etching, presumably second state of two with number trimmed off margin
caption: Merchants traded in the Royal Exchange’s open courtyard, moving under its arcades in wet weather. Thomas Gresham modeled this London centre of commerce on Antwerp’s Bourse.

title: Eyeglass Merchant
creator: After Adriaen van Ostade
caption: An eyeglass seller is the subject of this etching after Adriaen van Ostade. The museum retains a broad seventeenth-century date for the work.
sourceNote: Attributed after Adriaen van Ostade, not to him directly. Museum date: 1610–85; sortYear is only an approximate ordering value.

title: Massachusetts Shilling
creator: John Hull and Robert Sanderson
caption: A silver shilling from Boston, Massachusetts, dated 1652. The museum attributes its fabrication to John Hull and Robert Sanderson.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Shilling

title: The Goldsmith
creator: Rembrandt (Rembrandt van Rijn)
medium: Etching and drypoint; first of three states
caption: A craftsman works on a small figure of a mother with two children. Known as The Goldsmith, the scene brings the making of ornamental objects into view.

title: Jan Lutma, goldsmith
creator: Rembrandt (Rembrandt van Rijn)
medium: Etching, engraving and drypoint; first of four states
caption: The Amsterdam silversmith Jan Lutma sits with the tools and products of his trade: a hammer, chisels, a candlestick and a small dish.

title: The South Sea Scheme
creator: William Hogarth
medium: Etching and engraving; seventh state of seven
caption: A crowd gathers around a merry-go-round in Hogarth’s satire of the South Sea Bubble of 1720. Honour and Honesty are beaten while Trade sleeps.

title: Coins of the Qianlong Reign
creator: China, Qing dynasty
caption: A string of copper coins with square central holes. The museum places them in the Qianlong reign, 1736–95.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Coins

title: The Egg Merchant
creator: John Ingram; After François Boucher
caption: John Ingram depicts an egg seller in this etching and engraving after François Boucher. The Met dates the print to 1741–63.

title: Trade Card for a Textile Merchant
creator: Gabriel de Saint-Aubin
caption: A loom and ships appear behind the ornamental drapery of this textile merchant’s trade card. Saint-Aubin designed advertisements for artisans and businesses.

title: Four Mon Kan'ei Tsūhō Coin
creator: Japan, Edo period
caption: A copper four-mon coin from Edo-period Japan. The museum dates this example to 1768–1868.

title: The Tax Collectors (Les Traitants)
creator: Jean Honoré Fragonard
caption: This etching is known as The Tax Collectors, but the Met notes that its subject remains unverified. The title first appeared in an 1859 publication.
sourceNote: The museum states that the subject has never been verified; the historical title is retained without presenting the identification as certain.

title: "The Friend of the People" & his Petty New Tax Gatherer, Paying John Bull a Visit
creator: James Gillray
caption: Gillray pictures a visit from a tax gatherer in this hand-colored etching. The Met identifies Charles James Fox and Henry Petty-Fitzmaurice among its subjects.

title: Fish Merchant Carrying Yellowtails on Horseback
creator: Painting by Tani Bunchō; Inscription by Shokusanjin (Ōta Nanpo)
medium: Hanging scroll; ink and color on paper
caption: A fish merchant carries yellowtails on horseback in this Japanese hanging scroll. Tani Bunchō supplied the painting and Shokusanjin the inscription.

title: Banknote Motif: Fifty
creator: Associated with Cyrus Durand
caption: An engraved proof places the number 50 within a lace-like rondel of lathe-work ornament. The museum associates the design with Cyrus Durand.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Banknote motif: the number 50 against an ornamental lathe work rondel resembling lace

title: Banknote Motif: Six-Lobed Ornaments
creator: Associated with Cyrus Durand
medium: Engraving, printed in green ink; proof
caption: Two six-lobed lathe-work ornaments appear in this banknote-design proof. The engraving is printed in green ink and is associated with Cyrus Durand.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Banknote motif: two six-lobed lathe work ornaments

title: Design for Banknote
creator: Robert William Hume
medium: Pen and ink, brush and wash, graphite
caption: Hume developed this banknote design in pen and ink, brush and wash, and graphite. Its ornate border surrounds an open field and the denomination five.

title: Design for Banknote or Certificate
creator: Robert William Hume
caption: A design for a banknote or certificate, drawn in pen and ink, graphite, and watercolor. The museum dates Hume’s sheet to 1830–1900.

title: Tenpō Tsūhō Coin
creator: Japan, Edo period
caption: A copper Tenpō Tsūhō coin from Edo-period Japan. The museum dates this example to 1835–68.

title: Victoria and Una: Five Pound Piece
creator: William Wyon
caption: William Wyon’s gold five-pound piece pairs Victoria with Una. It was made for presentation and collectors rather than circulation.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Five Pound Piece: Victoria (obverse); Una (reverse)

title: A Banker in Barry Selly Cast, from Indian Trades and Castes
creator: Anonymous, Indian, 19th century
caption: Banking appears among the occupations represented in this Indian series of trades and castes.
sourceNote: The catalogue title is retained verbatim, including its historical terminology; the caption uses the museum’s broad identification of the depicted occupation.

title: The Tribute Money
creator: Eugène Delacroix
caption: Delacroix studied the biblical payment of the temple tax for a ceiling composition in the Palais Bourbon library. This 1843 graphite drawing formed part of that preparation.

title: A True View of a Trading House of a Yokohama Merchant
creator: Utagawa (Gountei) Sadahide
medium: Triptych of woodblock prints (nishiki-e); ink and color on paper; vertical ōban
caption: Merchants conduct business while workers carry goods through a Yokohama trading house. Sadahide’s triptych also records the encounter between Japanese and imported fashions.

title: Edward VII: Five Pound Piece
creator: George Edward de Saulles; after Benedetto Pistrucci
caption: A gold five-pound piece of 1902 pairs Edward VII with St. George and the dragon. The museum credits George Edward de Saulles and a design after Benedetto Pistrucci.
sourceNote: Museum catalogue title: Five Pound Piece: Edward VII (obverse); St. George and the Dragon (reverse)
